cohort: 6440 women who underwent hysterectomy at cesarean delivery for placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) from October 2015 to December 2018 in the US
finding: There is wide variation in the utilization of intra-arterial balloon occlusion at cesarean hysterectomy for PAS based on patient, pregnancy, and facility factors, suggesting a lack of universal practice guidelines.
mod_finding: Women who received intra-arterial balloon occlusion were more likely to have coagulopathy and arterial thrombosis in placenta accreta, but less likely to have hemorrhage in placenta increta, and blood transfusion and urinary tract injury in placenta percreta compared with those who did not.
gest_age: Early gestational age was associated with increased use of intra-arterial balloon occlusion
